summary: The migration from 908-line session-manager HTTP server to ~320-line per-invocation api-task-runner is well-executed with strong test coverage (32 passing tests) and solid security practices. Core architecture is sound: proper cleanup in finally blocks, platform-aware env allowlisting, Promise.race timeout handling, and correct return-based session lifecycle. All deleted files (session-manager.ts, types/session.ts, types/a2a-lite.ts) have no remaining references. The one-shot-runner.ts properly spawns api-task-runner as subprocess. Pipeline-config.ts and config-server.ts correctly removed session manager hooks. Web portal (app.js, index.html) has no session-related functionality. One minor nit: web/app.js lines 718-722 contain an empty '// Sessions' comment block that should be removed, but this is dead code with no functional impact.

findings.description: Lines 718-722 contain dead code: empty '// Sessions' section comment block with no implementation. This was likely left over from the session-manager removal. Should be removed to keep codebase clean but has no functional impact.
Line 6 comment reads 'Replaces the heavyweight session-manager HTTP server' - while historically accurate, could be reworded to focus on current functionality rather than historical context.
